Build Sequence
Phase 01

Concept & Regulation Study

Every DGP program starts on the regulation text, not the mood board. The technical group maps the current FIA framework before a single surface is drawn, so the car is legal by design rather than legal by correction.

Phase 02

Chassis & Aero Definition

Sidepod, floor, and wing geometry are developed together in CFD and the tunnel, so downforce gains in one area don't quietly cost the car somewhere else.

Phase 03

Livery & Identity

Colour, sponsor hierarchy, and surface graphics are locked only once the chassis geometry is final — the livery follows the car's real lines instead of covering them up.

Phase 04

Launch — Transcendence

The finished package, chassis, suit, and kit, is presented as a single system. Nothing on the car exists to be looked at in isolation.

Driver Equipment

Built for the cockpit.

The suit, kit, and paddock apparel carry the same visual system as the chassis, so the driver reads as part of the car.

01 / Race Wear

Race Suit & Helmet

Title partner branding across the chest and shoulders, with the DGP crest at the collar and car number on the helmet crown.

02 / Team Kit

Paddock Kit

Polo, softshell, and tee in matte black, carrying the full partner stack for pit wall and paddock wear.

03 / Accessories

Trousers & Cap

Utility trousers and the team cap close out the kit, finished with the same blue and yellow piping as the chassis.
